precepts.text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.
precepts.point: Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed”. The Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome.

“God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.” His power cannot be comprehended. Stop trying to figure the Creator out and questioning why he created what he created; you are the creation, so keep the commandments and play your role.

And notice: “Israel hath sinned”. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another.

precepts.text: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice.
precepts.point: Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.” We cannot find him out; he is excellent in power and in judgment, and his justice is plenty. That is who made Israel turn their backs before Ai, and you are not going to figure him out.

His judgment here is on the whole house: they have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff; the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins.

“neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.” What is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it. Keep the commandments and play your role.

precepts.text: When we bring tithes, which is food, to Jerusalem, you give the tenth part that the Lord blessed you with; that tenth part is the mercy that He shows us.
precepts.point: Rain also comes for the land's sake; the land needs to be watered, vegetation needs to grow. And waters and rain also come for mercy's sake.

note.label: Job 37: The Works of the Most High

precepts.why:
“He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.” The flood during Noah's time came for correction; the rain and the hail around Egypt's time came for correction. Rain also comes for the land's sake, because the land needs to be watered and vegetation needs to grow. And waters and rain also come for mercy's sake.

“And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is the Lord’s: it is holy unto the Lord.” When we bring tithes, which is food, to Jerusalem, you give the tenth part that the Lord blessed you with, the seed of the land and the fruit of the tree that his rain brought forth. That tenth part is the mercy that he shows us, and it is holy unto the Lord.

points: The winds, the frost, the waters, everything comes whether for correction, or for His land, or for mercy.
Rain also comes for the land's sake; the land needs to be watered, vegetation needs to grow. And waters and rain also come for mercy's sake.

note.label: Job 37: The Works of the Most High

points: Hearken unto this, O Job; stand still and consider the wondrous works of God. Consider the wondrous works of Him which is perfect in knowledge, how thy garments are warm when He quieteth the earth by the south wind.

note.label: Job 37: The Works of the Most High

points: He spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass. Teach us what we shall say unto Him, for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.

note.label: Job 37: The Works of the Most High

points: God is terrible with majesty. Touching the Almighty, we cannot find Him out; He is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice, and He will not afflict.

note.label: Job 37: The Works of the Most High

points: Men do therefore fear Him. He respecteth not any that are wise of heart. So it does not matter how much knowledge you have; there is still no respect of persons with the Lord.
